source.title: Supervised sparse auto-encoders for interpretable and compositional representations
source.authors: Ouns El Harzli; Hugo Wallner; Yoonsoo Nam; Haixuan Xavier Tao

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses unconstrained-feature-model geometry as theoretical motivation for its supervised SAE, but does not measure superposition geometry or test the claim versions. Its reported results concern the performance of its own feature-editing method.
record.gate_note: The paper argues that training may decorrelate concept subspaces, but reports no measurement of their angles, overlap, sparsity-dependent transition, or capacity competition. Its composition and editing results are method outcomes, not tests of the claim versions. The cited findings about unsupervised SAEs are from other work and are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper builds a supervised, decoder-only SAE with predefined concept blocks on Stable Diffusion 3.5 prompt embeddings. It reports only its own method's editing and composition outcomes, judged by visual inspection. It does not measure superposition geometry, capacity competition, polysemanticity, or whether unsupervised SAE features are canonical units. Features are imposed by supervision, not discovered, so the results cannot bear on V4 or V5. Decorrelation of concept subspaces is argued from theory but never measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that their decoder-only supervised SAE avoids the L1 penalty and gives concept-aligned directions. Preliminary Stable Diffusion 3.5 results show compositional generalisation and feature-level modular editing. Decorrelation of concept subspaces is offered only as a theoretical argument.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a decoder-only supervised SAE with predefined sparse concept blocks, shared learnable concept sub-vectors, and prompt-embedding reconstruction; it does not use the original toy-model superposition setup or measure its geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: A supervised concept-block SAE swapped hair colour into unseen concept combinations. The intended change was judged present in 100% of more than 50 inspected images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised SAEs with predefined concept subspaces support compositional editing of diffusion prompt embeddings for some unseen concept combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature-level edits sometimes altered image content other than the targeted concept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-level interventions in supervised prompt-embedding SAEs can have off-target effects.

record.problems: The authors describe the experiments as preliminary and limited by computational constraints. Evaluation is limited to Stable Diffusion 3.5 prompt embeddings, and the quantified hair-color result is based on visual inspection of >50 images for a task the authors note may be easy. The study reports no comparison against state-of-the-art editing methods and does not measure the proposed concept-subspace geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Other concept removals, insertions, and swaps are illustrated qualitatively in Figures 2–7, without separately reported numerical outcomes.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, no measured geometry, no sparsity transition.
All of it: capacity competition and dedicated dimensions are not studied.
All of it: alternative causes of polysemanticity are not studied.
All of it: the SAE is supervised with predefined concepts, so no sparse features are recovered from LLMs.
All of it: completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are only cited from other work (Leask et al.). They are not tested here.
All of it: d=10 concept subspaces are a design choice, not a test of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification is confirmed. Statements about unsupervised SAEs (entanglement, absorption, non-canonical units) are cited from other work and were rightly not recorded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test overcomplete toy networks, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Does not test feature distribution across LLM neurons or SAE recovery of sparse features in LLMs.
Uses predefined supervised concept blocks, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses concept subspaces of dimension d = 10, but does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large Turbo
rows.stage_stated: inference only; diffusion model parameters not fine-tuned or modified
rows.operation_detail: Swapped hair-color concepts in the trained sparse latent representation, decoded the prompt embedding, and generated images.

conditions.value: change hair color from brune to blond in configurations where blond hair and blue eyes were absent from training

rows.measure: Images judged to show the intended hair-color change
rows.note: Aggregate result for the specific hair-color task. This measures the supervised method's editing outcome, not spontaneous superposition or any listed claim version.
rows.check: This row measures the study's own method's editing success: hair-colour swaps judged visually in over 50 images. That is a method outcome, not a measure of superposition. The authors note the task may be 'easy'. There is no baseline or control.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large Turbo
rows.stage_stated: inference only; diffusion model parameters not fine-tuned or modified
rows.operation_detail: Applied concept removal, insertion, and swapping in the trained sparse latent representation and generated images.

conditions.value: feature-level modular edits; specific evaluation set not stated

rows.measure: Whether edits affected only the targeted visual concept
rows.value: The transformations were not always neutral with respect to the rest of the image.
rows.note: The paper gives no rate or specific examples for this spillover result. It does not establish that the effect is caused by superposition.
rows.check: This is a qualitative limitation of the method, with no rate and no attributed cause. It is not a measure of superposition.

relation.reason: Uses sparse concept representations for interventions without testing superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, dictionary completeness or canonicality, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: Reports its supervised SAE method's composition and editing outcomes. Predefined concept blocks impose semantic structure; the experiments do not test any listed superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: The 100% result is visual assessment of more than 50 hair-color edits; the authors describe this as potentially easy. Spillover has no reported rate, and concept-subspace decorrelation is a theoretical argument rather than an experimental measurement.
